 C482 No.1031 of 2024
 Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1.
Mr. Girish Chandra Lakhchaura, learned counsel for the applicant.
2. Mr. Saurabh Pandey, learned Brief Holder for the State.

3. By the instant C482 application, the present applicant is challenging the proceeding of Complaint Case No.2056 of 2020, wherein the present applicant has been summoned for the offences punishable under Sections 323, 498-A and 506 of IPC read with Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, in FIR No.230 of 2019, pending in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Khatima,
Udham Singh Nagar.

entities.text: Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Khatima
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant married with respondent no.2- complainant on 22.01.2019, but, due to some differences, they are living separately since 14.06.2019.

Subsequently, the FIR was lodged by the respondent on 08.09.2019, in which after investigation, the charge- sheet was filed against the applicant for the offence punishable under Sections 323, 498A, 506 of IPC read with Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act in which the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate took cognizance on 27.08.2020 and on 12.02.2024, the trial Court framed the charges against the applicant.
5.

In addition to this, the respondent no.2 initiated a proceeding under Section 125 Cr.P.C by moving an application for maintenance and the Judge Family Court Khatima by order dated 23.11.2022 granted interim maintenance of Rupees 3,000/- per month to the respondent, which was challenged by the present applicant in Criminal Revision No.218 of 2023 and this Court refer the parties for mediation by order dated 04.01.2024, and, thereafter, both the parties appear before the mediator and the mediator submits its report on 04.01.2024 by observing that both the parties have settled their dispute amicably and decided to dissolve their marriage by way of mutual consent by filing a petition under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act.
The copy of written settlement as arrived between the parties before the mediator is also enclosed which is the part of report of the mediator.

C482/1031/2024 on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102595888/
1 6.
I have also perused the settlement arrived in between the parties and it appears from the settlement that the applicant was agreed to pay a sum of Rupees 14,00,000/- towards permanent alimony.
Out of which, a demand draft of Rupees 5 lakhs i.e. D.D. No.635995 was given to the respondent wife on 08.01.2024.
It is also mentioned in para 7 of the settlement that both the parties will get divorce by way of mutual consent.

Thereafter, a petition was filed under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act by both the parties, which was registered as Family Case No.9124 of 2024 before the Judge Family Court , Khatima, Udham Singh Nagar on 09.01.2024.

entities.text: Judge Family Court , Khatima, Udham Singh Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner is aggrieved with the statement as recorded by the Family Court of the respondent-wife, wherein she once again repeating the allegations which she has alleged in the FIR.

7. It is also submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that once the settlement has been arrived and it was agreed that a total sum of rupees 14,00,000/-(Rupees Fourteen Lakhs only) will be paid towards permanent alimony out of which Rupees five lakh has been paid through demand draft, but thereafter the respondent complainant takes u turn while giving her statement in Criminal Case no.2056 of 2020.

He further submits that the conduct of respondent complainant appears to be malicious particularly when the parties have settled their dispute and the petition has been filed under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act.

8. Mr. Saurabh Pandey, learned Brief Holder fairly submits that once the settlement has been arrived in between the parties and the part payment has been made of the amount as settled towards the permanent alimony, then in such a situation respondent complainant should comply the terms and condition as settled between the parties.
9. All these aspects required to be considered after inviting counter- affidavit.
10. Issue notice to respondent no.2.
11.
Respondent may file counter- affidavit within four weeks.
Two weeks' time thereafter is also granted to the counsel for the applicant to file rejoinder affidavit.

12. List this matter on 23.07.2024.
13.
In the meantime, further proceeding of Complaint Case No.2056 of 2020, pending in the Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Khatima, Udham Singh Nagar, Dehradun shall remain stayed.
